skill.displayName: Workplace Group Stress Heatmap | 职场员工压力群体热力图

version.changelog:
- Updated to version 1.0.7.
- Documentation improvements: SKILL.md revised; outdated skill-card.md file removed.
- No changes to core logic or features—documentation only.

llm.summary: This skill performs sensitive workplace camera stress analysis through external cloud APIs and silently links use to a persistent local or remote identity, so it should receive careful review before installation.

dimensions.detail: The runtime reads local video files or accepts video URLs, sends the analysis request to configured lifeemergence.com services, and retrieves cloud report history; this is proportionate only for an approved workplace-monitoring deployment with explicit consent and data handling controls.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: No separate installer, autorun hook, or executable permission change was found; dependencies are ordinary Python packages, but runtime scripts are intended to be invoked directly and call network services.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The skill declares default triggering for office-camera videos and automatic cloud history queries, and instructs the agent not to ask for or reveal internal identity values even though those values are used to associate reports.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: The code reads a workspace data/smyx-api-key.txt identity if present, otherwise creates and reuses a local SQLite sys_user record, can silently register/login with that identity, stores returned tokens, and attaches identity/auth headers and pnaUserName to API requests.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

dimensions.detail: The stated workplace group-stress heatmap purpose is coherent with video analysis, heatmap reports, and cloud report retrieval, but it is high-impact employee monitoring involving facial-expression and posture inference from office camera footage.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

llm.guidance: Install only in an organization-approved deployment where employees have been notified and consent or another lawful basis is documented. Confirm where video, reports, identifiers, and tokens are stored, who can retrieve historical reports, and whether the external service retention and access controls meet your workplace privacy requirements.
llm.findings:
[AST7] unexpected: Verified dynamic getattr-based DAO filtering in shared list/count helpers; it is a real robustness issue but not material to this verdict because the reviewed skill path does not expose arbitrary filter dictionaries to end users.
[LP3] expected: Local file access and network calls are expected for cloud-backed video analysis, but the artifact does not provide a crisp permissions and data-flow boundary for the external upload, identity use, and report retrieval.
[SDI-1] expected: Persistent identity is documented as internal report association, but it weakens the skill's repeated anonymous framing and should be reviewed in the context of employee-monitoring data.
[SDI-4] expected: The no-identity language appears aimed at employees in the footage, while the implementation still performs user/account identity handling; that distinction is not prominent enough for this sensitive use case.
[SDI-2] expected: Generic API helpers and identity bootstrap code are present in shared modules; the cloud API path is purpose-aligned, but the broad helper surface and automatic identity behavior increase review risk.
[SQP-1] expected: The broad default and history-query triggers match the documented workflow, but they are risky for sensitive workplace footage and historical organizational-health reports without explicit confirmation.
[SQP-2] expected: The skill includes some privacy and consent notes, but the code can upload local office video or submit a remote video URL for external analysis without a runtime consent gate.
[E1] expected: External transmission is verified for silent login/registration and API requests; it is not malicious by itself, but it is material because identity-bearing data is sent in a skill marketed around anonymous workplace analytics.
